findings: 様 is more deferential than さん. The 1952 guidance treats 様 as formal/address use and さん as standard; the 2001 report describes context and field variation, not a simple universal ranking.

様 is especially common in customer service, business mail and formal documents. The sources support formal correspondence/address and contextual variation but do not quantify customer-service frequency.
様 should not ordinarily be added to one’s own name. No exact primary locator was found for self-reference.
All article examples and contrasts are current and generalizable. The report warns that role-title honorific acceptability varies by field; examples remain editorial and uncited.
